reusedRecord.canonicalName: Cadillac Resolution Opposing Wexford Water Technologies Injection-Well Permit.pdf
reusedRecord.resolution: The supplied file is an exact byte match; the established record is reused as a cross-reference and no duplicate is published.

verifiedFindings: PDF page 3 states that Cadillac had treated Wexford County Landfill leachate for over 20 years.
PDF page 3 states that Cadillac safely treated and discharged 14 million gallons of leachate in 2016 and had the ability to safely treat and discharge up to 20 million gallons annually.

PDF page 3 lists cadmium, lead, nickel, chromium, arsenic, benzene, ethylbenzene, ammonia, silver, copper and toluene as contaminants treated and removed through the City's IPP and wastewater treatment plant.
PDF page 4 states that contaminants were safely removed and clean water was discharged under EPA- and MDEQ-prescribed NPDES permit limits.
The separate official minutes record unanimous approval of motion 2017-232 to adopt a resolution with the same title and permit number.
evidentiaryBoundary: The supplied PDF's resolution number, mover, seconder, vote, adoption date and certification fields are blank. It is therefore retained as draft resolution text, while the official minutes establish Council action. Its volume, duration, capacity and removal statements are municipal assertions and do not replace underlying delivery logs, DMR totals, capacity calculations, analytical results or treatment-removal measurements.

queueResolution.reason: The reused draft adds municipal duration, volume, capacity and contaminant-treatment assertions, but it does not establish an exact final delivery date, provide load-level receiving history, supply PFAS analytical evidence or prove a source-to-receptor migration pathway.
